### Review

Review is Forgejo's pull request review: approve, or request changes and say what must change; a comment neither approves nor holds anything. A pull request into `main` of `paper-repo` waits for the owners of the paths it changes, and one into its `release` or `final` waits for the approval of `internal-review-repo`, the only one counted there, of the very commit it merges: a push to it after the approval withdraws it. A review request stands until its reviewer reviews, and a review until its reviewer reviews again: nobody withdraws or dismisses another's.

### Versions and release

A version for the world's users is a merge of `main` into `release` of `paper-repo`, by a pull request that `internal-review-repo` approved and whose checks pass. The system writes the checks as commit statuses on the pull request's head (`hutian/delivery`, and the world's contract's when it holds one), and a failing one says what is missing and who provides it; nobody else writes a status. Merge with a merge commit, not a squash or a rebase, or the next version conflicts. The system publishes each version as a release of `world/result`, the world's results, with the delivery attached: the users of the world read those releases and nothing else, and every role reads them. The last approval is a merge into `final` in the same way: the system releases the world from it, at once, and nothing pushed after it is part of it. Offer a `release` version as soon as the delivery holds its main work, so that `internal-review-repo`'s review comes while there is still room to act on it; `final` is the last. Do not ask another role to review the same unchanged delivery twice merely to pass through both branches. A release goes to the world's user; no role submits it to a venue or declares a licence for it.

When the world is quiet, the system hands each remaining gap of the delivery to its owner once, and once more when `main` of `paper-repo` has moved since; if it goes quiet again before a gap, a version, an open request or a review changes, the world ends there, unless a tracked job is still running, or the world runs to a wall-clock limit with someone outside attending it and all that is left is that `paper-repo` has proposed no version, with nothing failed and nothing open but requests that `ht-human` opened and their owners have seen: then it waits instead of ending, up to that limit. So whatever needs another role's action must be open where that role owns it.

Leaderboards built from pairwise comparisons, such as Chatbot Arena, publish Bradley--Terry scores with bootstrap confidence intervals. An interval says how far the ranking moves under resampling, not how many of the existing comparisons a conclusion such as ``model $a$ is above model $b$'' rests on, or whether that number is large for data of that size and spread. We measure the smallest number of comparisons whose deletion, or whose outcome change, reverses a conclusion (a verified upper bound found by search), express it in standard-error units, and compare it with the same quantity on data simulated from the dataset's own fitted model. On crowd votes, expert labels, LLM-judge labels of the same battles and basketball seasons, the real count lies within a pre-set margin of that reference wherever there are enough pairs to decide; outcome flips on Arena are within the margin but not on it. Random noise of the size of the smallest adversarial change essentially never reverses a conclusion, yet separated confidence intervals do not survive small targeted changes. Matched comparisons of crowd, expert and model-judge labels on identical items show no design-specific departure beyond the margin. A regression on separation, size, density and ties predicts the count for held-out datasets about as well as a simulation does, and less well for a held-out design. Design is confounded with dataset, so every claim concerns the instances studied.
\section{Experiments}\label{sec:experiments}

Table~\ref{tab:data} lists the \nSets{} datasets: the Arena-55k crowd votes (64 models) and their single-turn subset; \nJudges{} LLM judges that re-labelled the \emph{same} single-turn battles (verdict from position-averaged probabilities, ties as the judge returns them); MT-Bench expert and GPT-4 judgments of the same questions and answer pairs, GPT-4 also restricted to the pairs the experts judged; and \nNBA{} NBA regular seasons (franchises, game outcomes, no ties). I checked the numbers and what the text says each one is against the code and `results/*.csv` for the commit `f00d642`. `make_numbers.py` reads the tables, and the Table 2 values (strata, Q, Q null, SE ratio real and null, Arena 33/70/155 and 0.057%/0.27%) agree with `fragility_by_z.csv` and `se_ratio.csv`. `nBootCore`=500 and 91 data sets agree with `datasets_computed.csv`. Four points where the text says something other than what was computed:

1. **Positive control is missing from the text.** The PR body says the claim about what Δ can detect is worded conditionally, but I find no sentence saying so (grep for "control"/"detect" in the sections gives only "we therefore detect no design-specific departure"). Without the control, "no departure beyond ±0.15" reads as evidence of absence. Until the control (#9, six jobs, running) is delivered, add one sentence in Sections 5.1/5.3 and the Discussion: "whether Δ would detect a departure of a given size was not tested on these data in this version". I will post the sizes when the jobs end, which replaces that sentence.
2. **SE-ratio sentence (experiments.tex, "Design or statistics").** It says the published interval "differs between datasets at equal Q" and lists 0.81 (crowd), 1.00, 1.05, 1.30. shown.message:
I reviewed `paper-repo`#10 and requested changes, mainly because the paper has no sentence about the positive control that is still running.

Numbers and Table 2 match my result tables. The four things that don't:
- **Control not mentioned:** the paper says "no departure beyond ±0.15" without saying the control hasn't been run yet. I asked for one sentence saying so until the results arrive.
- **SE ratio:** the crowd 0.81 is a tie effect that the same-graph null also shows (0.82). Only MT-Bench expert's 1.30 is a design effect. The 0.88–1.16 range needs the words "relative to the same-graph simulation".
- **Random noise at k\*:** the "no random draw reversed a pair" sentence holds only for deletion and z in [1,8]. It sits next to a Table 5 figure computed on all sampled conclusions, so the scope needs stating.
- **f_q/f_adv bounds:** they come from the formula, so the text should say so.

The positive-control jobs are still running (Arena overdisp, position, cyclic and pairdev; MT-Bench human). #7 and #9 stay open until I can run `scripts/15_control_table.py` and report the detection sizes.
